newsitem.title: NORWAY: Braathens' new route seen to break even in '98.
newsitem.headline: Braathens' new route seen to break even in '98.

text.p: The loss-making Oslo-Stockholm route of Norwegian airliner Braathens SAFE should break even next year, according to a NatWest Securities company update released on Thursday.

It said Braathens' first-quarter results presented three weeks ago fell short of those for the first quarter of 1996 because of start-up costs on the new Oslo-Stockholm route and losses at domestic Swedish carrier Transwede Airways.
"However trading conditions will improve through the year and the new route should break even in 1998," NatWest said.
It forecast that Transwede would break even this year.
Braathens last November launched regular flights between Oslo and Stockholm and has said it plans a further offensive in the region including a frequent-flyer programme linked to British Airways.
Braathens owns half of Transwede and holds an option to buy the remaining 50 percent before the end of this year.
NatWest said Braathens, through its Nordic alliance, was an increasingly credible rival to the traditional dominance of Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) in the region.
Last month Braathens, Finland's Finnair and Transwede announced plans to increase co-operation in a move seen as an attack on SAS domination of the Nordic.
"Given the stock's attractive valuation relative to its peers, we reiterate our Add recommendation," the update said.

Mainly because of the new Stockholm route, Braathens' revenue from international routes increased to 89 million crowns from 64 million. But net expenses linked to the Stockholm run were about 17 million crowns for the first quarter.
